subject: Martin Luther King Jr. Day Celebration
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted a community celebration honoring Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., featuring musical performances, community discussions, and keynote remarks on civil rights and local history. The event also recognized several local leaders with the center's 2023 Drum Major Awards.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Invocation
items.summary: Director of Elder Services Tariq Carter opened the event, followed by an invocation from Rabbi Jessica Delera Nussbaum connecting Dr. King's work to the biblical story of Exodus.

items.title: Executive Director Address
items.summary: Executive Director Lisa Crossman discussed the history and mission of the West Medford Community Center and emphasized the importance of community volunteerism.

items.title: Mayor's Remarks
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn spoke on Dr. King's enduring relevance and outlined city initiatives focused on diversity, equity, and public advocacy.

items.title: Musical Performance: Bridge Over Troubled Water
items.summary: Stacey Clayton performed a vocal rendition of 'Bridge Over Troubled Water.'

items.title: Reading of Letter from Birmingham Jail
items.summary: Tariq Carter and Maya Carter performed an abridged dramatic reading of Dr. King's 1963 'Letter from Birmingham Jail.'

items.title: 2023 Drum Major Award Presentations
items.summary: The West Medford Community Center presented 2023 Drum Major Awards to David Cha, Richard Trotter, Superintendent Dr. Marice-Edouard Vincent, and posthumously to Edward 'Buddy' Clayton.

items.title: Musical Performance: Healing Waters
items.summary: Max Heineck and Linda Moreau performed the original musical composition 'Healing Waters.'

items.title: Community Table Discussions and Reports
items.summary: Attendees held table discussions addressing community issues, local history, and school race relations, followed by representative group reports.

items.title: Keynote Address
items.summary: Royall House and Slave Quarters Executive Director Kiara Singleton delivered a keynote address reflecting on Dr. King's radical activism and the history of enslaved people in Medford.

items.title: Poem Presentation: A Call to Action
items.summary: Medford Poet Laureate Terry Carter recited his original poem 'A Call to Action.'

items.title: Reflections on the Beloved Community
items.summary: Reverend David M. Kilpatrick shared personal memories of meeting Dr. King and offered reflections on building a beloved community.

items.title: Closing Song and Final Remarks
items.summary: Stacey Clayton led attendees in singing 'Lift Every Voice and Sing,' followed by final remarks and acknowledgments from Executive Director Lisa Crossman.
